gen-gf-revalia-gf-noto-sans-nushu: Revalia swaggers in with a tall band of letters and a loose, relaxed stride between them. Noto Sans Nushu is the quieter one, with terminals held far from the stroke and a towering x-height.
gen-gf-revalia-gf-noto-sans-ogham: Clean and contemporary, the body lines look bold because the lowercase bodies stand so tall, while Revalia loves a loose, expressive stride. Noto Sans Ogham keeps wide gaps in its e.
gen-gf-revalia-gf-noto-sans-ol-chiki: Noto Sans Ol Chiki sets words as solid blocks, not skylines. Revalia is the showman, spacing its bold letters apart and leaving the g's lower curve open, while the sans body holds its curve tails well back from the stroke.
gen-gf-revalia-gf-noto-sans-old-hungaria: Noto Sans Old Hungarian reads friendly and open, even tiny. Its big counters in a, e and s stay clear while Revalia's bold, widely spaced display letters add the loud, expressive swagger.
gen-gf-revalia-gf-noto-sans-old-italic: Noto Sans Old Italic reads tight and businesslike, with almost no gap between x-height and cap height and curve endings held apart. Revalia handles the loud, expressive display work; the sans-serif body simply gets on with being tidy.
gen-gf-revalia-gf-noto-sans-old-north-ar: Revalia's lowercase g leaves its lower curve open. Pair that with Noto Sans Old North Arabian, dense and tall in the lowercase with outward-pointing terminals like tongs, and a bold display meets a compact, approachable sans.
gen-gf-revalia-gf-noto-sans-old-permic: Loud up top, friendly below. Revalia stretches its bold letters out in a relaxed stride; Noto Sans Old Permic has rounded forms open to the side, and lowercase nearly as tall as its capitals, so a modest size should hold up.
gen-gf-revalia-gf-noto-sans-old-persian: That open lower curve on Revalia's g gives its bold, widely spaced letters a relaxed, expressive swagger across the line. Noto Sans Old Persian answers with lofty lowercase and counters that breathe.
gen-gf-revalia-gf-noto-sans-old-sogdian: Revalia's tall band of letters, topped by short stalks, sets the bold, expressive tone. Noto Sans Old Sogdian is the strongest half, its tall x-height nearly reaching cap height and wide-mouthed letters staying crisp when shrunk.
gen-gf-revalia-gf-noto-sans-old-turkic: Revalia strides across the line with widely separated letters and a g whose lower curve stays open, loud and expressive. Noto Sans Old Turkic is chunky, tall and approachable.
